data.title: Ford, Honda, Stellantis, VW sue New Jersey to block 'extortionate' vehicle repair law
data.description: Nov 20 : Ford, Honda, Stellantis' FCA unit and Volkswagen sued New Jersey on Friday to block a new state law they say increases the amounts automakers must pay franchised dealers for warranty and recall repairs. In a complaint filed in federal court in Trenton, New Jersey, the automakers said the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Open Recall Notice and Fair Compensation Act gives dealers a "blank check" to set prices for warranty, recall and other repair services, while prohibiting manufacturers from avoiding "extortionate" results or recovering the costs. New Jersey's law will shift more than $375 million a year to dealers from automakers, giving dealers a "windfall" by imposing no obligation to use the money to improve customer service or boost compensation for employees, the automakers said. "In short, the act rewards dealers for charging their customers more," the automakers said. The office of New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, who enforces the state's laws, did not immediately respond to requests for comment. New Jersey's law took effect on April 1, after former Governor Phil Murphy signed it in September 2025. CONSTITUTIONAL VIOLATIONS ALLEGED The automakers objected to letting dealers charge a "labor multiplier" based on samples of repair orders, saying it lets dealers bill for substantially more labor time than they actually work. They also challenged provisions requiring automakers to pay marked-up prices on parts that the dealers received at reduced cost or for free, and preventing automakers from providing less expensive parts even if supply, demand or other factors justified price cuts. Ford, Honda, FCA — which includes Fiat and Chrysler — and Volkswagen said that since the law took effect, each has received dozens of bills requiring payment "for hours that no technician works, that surpass what comparable dealers charge for the same work, and that exceed what retail customers pay." They said the law violates the US Constitution's Commerce Clause and Takings Clause, is preempted by federal law governing recalls, and violates New Jersey's Constitution. The nonprofit New Jersey Coalition of Automotive Retailers is also a defendant. It did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: Honda to recall 810,000 US vehicles over Takata air bag rupture risk
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 20 : Honda said on Friday it is recalling 810,592 older cars and SUVs in the US over a risk that Takata air bag inflators could rupture. The recall includes some 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles that were originally sold or registered in 14 states or territories known for high temperature, humidity and large temperature fluctuations. Honda said there no injuries or crashes tied to the vehicles being recalled, and there have been no air bag inflator ruptures. But the company's long-term monitoring and analysis revealed potential propellant degradation in certain inflators within specific geographic regions, it said. There have been at least 28 deaths in the United States stemming from defective Takata air bag inflators since 2009, an issue that prompted the largest auto recall in US history. Over the past decade, two dozen major automakers have recalled more than 100 million vehicles fitted with Takata airbag inflators worldwide, including about 67 million vehicles in the United States. Various automakers have also reported hundreds of injuries in vehicles since 2009 from Takata air bag inflators that can explode, unleashing metal shrapnel inside cars and trucks, killing or injuring drivers or other vehicle occupants. The vehicles in the new recall have air bags inflators that contain a moisture-absorbing material — unlike the millions of vehicles recalled previously. The recall applies to vehicles sold or registered in Alabama, California, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Louisiana, Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas, Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan), Guam and American Samoa.

data.title: CrowdStrike in talks to acquire Zscaler, sources say
data.description: Nov 20 : CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire cybersecurity provider and rival Zscaler amid consolidation in the security software sector, according to two people familiar with the matter. The talks between the two companies are ongoing, the sources said. No deal is guaranteed, and the discussions could still end without an agreement, the people added. Shares of Zscaler, which has a market capitalization of around $33.5 billion, jumped 17 per cent in after-hours trading on Friday. CrowdStrike shares fell 8 per cent. A combination would create one of the world's largest pure-play cybersecurity providers as enterprise customers seek to reduce the number of security vendors they use, favoring providers that can deliver multiple products through a single relationship. CrowdStrike and Zscaler did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. CrowdStrike's Falcon platform is widely used to secure endpoints such as laptops, servers and mobile devices, while Zscaler specializes in cloud-based network security services that help companies securely connect users to applications without relying on traditional corporate networks. Founded in 2011 by Chief Executive George Kurtz, CrowdStrike has grown into one of the world's largest cybersecurity companies, helping organizations detect and respond to cyber threats through its cloud-native software platform. The Austin, Texas-based company has expanded beyond endpoint protection through acquisitions and internal development into areas including cloud, identity and threat intelligence security. The deal would address one of CrowdStrike's biggest gaps in network security and help it compete more directly with platform providers such as Palo Alto Networks.

data.title: Cognition in talks for new funding at $75 billion valuation, Bloomberg News reports
data.description: Nov 20 : Coding startup Cognition AI is in funding talks at a $75 billion valuation, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. The company is considering raising $2 billion or more in the latest round, the report said, adding that the talks were ongoing and the details could change. The news comes about two months after Cognition raised $2 billion in a Series E funding round at a valuation of $48 billion. The round was led by new investors Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, alongside existing backers Founders Fund, General Catalyst, and Avenir. Cognition did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The company is an AI startup that develops autonomous software-engineering agents, which can plan, write, test and deploy code with limited human intervention. The company was valued at $26 billion in a funding round in May, when it raised $1 billion.

data.title: GTA VI books record $3.79 billion in sales on first day of launch
data.description: Nov 20 : "Grand Theft Auto VI" recorded $3.79 billion in retail sales in the first 24 hours of its launch, developer Rockstar Games said on Friday, cementing its position as the world's biggest videogame release of all time.

data.title: YouTube nears $3 billion settlement with US school districts over addiction claims, Bloomberg News reports
data.description: Nov 20 : YouTube has reached an in-principle agreement to potentially pay about $3 billion to thousands of US school districts that accused it of designing an addictive platform that harmed students' mental health, Bloomberg News reported on Friday. The deal also includes product safeguards for teens and is contingent on a majority of districts signing on, with finalization likely to take a few months, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. Any settlement would have to be approved by US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland, California, who is overseeing the litigation. The districts, ranging from New York City and Los Angeles to smaller communities, have also sued Meta Platforms, Snap and TikTok, alleging that features such as recommendation algorithms, autoplay and infinite scroll were designed to hook young users and contributed to depression, anxiety and eating disorders. The companies have denied the claims. YouTube parent Alphabet did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment. Unlike the other platforms, YouTube has been broadly adopted by schools for classroom use. A September survey of more than 2,000 high-school students by the Thomas B. Fordham Institute found that over 30 per cent used YouTube for entertainment rather than teacher-directed activities during the school day. The schools say they have had to spend money enforcing phone bans and hiring mental-health staff, and they are seeking funds and platform changes. The next federal school trial, involving Tucson, Arizona, is set for February, with Meta, TikTok and Snap still defendants, the report added.  In August, Meta agreed to pay up to $18 billion over the next decade and strictly limit how teenagers use Facebook and Instagram to settle claims by nearly all US states that it designed its platforms to addict children.

data.title: Robinhood faces shareholder challenge as SEC loosens proxy oversight
data.description: Nov 20 : A shareholder activist group called for online brokerage Robinhood to review its proxy-voting platform, concerned that retail investors aren't getting fair choices as financial regulators weaken balloting rules for corporate annual meetings. Robinhood and its Say investor-communications arm are at the center of changes coming to contests like director elections or CEO pay approvals. Robinhood worked with Tesla to create a way for retail investors to cast their ballots automatically that won approval from the US Securities and Exchange Commission in September. Backers say such retail-voting plans will increase retail investors' voting participation rates, even as the SEC takes steps that could eliminate shareholder proposals at corporate meetings. Critics say Tesla and others like ExxonMobil are designing their programs to unfairly channel votes in favor of management recommendations. A shareholder resolution filed with Robinhood for its next annual meeting, seen by Reuters, could spark debate about the role of investor rights. In the resolution the activist group As You Sow says Robinhood limits customers to using its own voting platform that requires a "painstaking and time-consuming challenge" to vote on individual corporate ballot items, rather than using third-party voting services. It also notes Robinhood's work with Tesla's management-friendly voting option. The limited voting choices create legal and reputational risks, said As You Sow in its resolution, which calls for Robinhood to review offering clients more ways to vote, "including an independent voting service of their choice." As You Sow leaders said ideally Robinhood might offer something like Vanguard's voting program which casts prorated shares of funds' votes according to investors' preferences. Vanguard clients can select among voting policies like one that tends to support environmental and social shareholder resolutions, or one that supports management recommendations. Robinhood "shouldn't be limiting choices," said Danielle Fugere, As You Sow president, in an interview. "You should get to choose. That's what voting is all about." Robinhood representatives did not respond to messages seeking comment.

data.title: Wall Street regulator proposes to take control of market surveillance tool
data.description: Nov 20 : The US Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday proposed taking direct control of a comprehensive market surveillance tool long the subject of funding and privacy complaints, the agency announced. The proposal makes good on the Trump administration's longstanding pledge to rework the so-called Consolidated Audit Trail, which the agency mandated following the 2010 "flash crash," in which Wall Street indices temporarily erased nearly $1 trillion in market value in minutes. The surveillance system remains the only source of its kind for comprehensive data and information about market events, making it crucial to investigations into market conduct including insider trading and market manipulation. The SEC has cited CAT data in the prosecution of an alleged $47 million front-running scheme, for example. But investment industry and stock market operators have battled over who should foot the bill for its development and operations costs while conservative critics decry what they say is the CAT's invasive collection of market participants' personal data. The system is currently operated by an organization overseen by the industry-funded Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. But under Friday's proposal stock exchanges and broker-dealers themselves would collect and report the same data to the agency or its designee, giving the SEC direct control, the agency said. SEC Chair Paul Atkins said in Friday's statement that this would make the CAT "accountable in its governance and disciplined in its costs," to the benefit of both markets and market participants. The announcement confirmed that the Trump administration had stepped back from conservatives' most aggressive moves. The manifesto known as "Project 2025," to which Atkins was a contributor, called for the CAT's outright elimination. When the system was formally adopted in 2016, then-SEC Commissioner Kara Stein referred to it as a potential "Hubble Telescope" for securities markets.

data.title: Mexican cell carriers facing widespread outages, users report
data.description: MEXICO CITY, Nov 20 : Mexican cellphone users reported widespread service outages on Friday affecting Telcel, AT&T Mexico and Movistar, marking the latest disruption to mobile networks in the country. Users began reporting problems around 11 a.m. local time, including an inability to make calls, loss of cellular signal and problems accessing mobile data, according to outage-tracking platform Downdetector. • Telcel is controlled by America Movil, while Movistar remains operated by Spain's Telefonica while its sale to US consortium Melisa Acquisition is underway • Spokespeople for America Movil, AT&T Mexico and Movistar did not immediately respond to requests for comment • Mexico's Commission for Telecommunications Regulation (CRT) also did not immediately respond to a Reuters request • The disruption comes just over a month after users reported outages in mid-October including loss of cellular signal and problems with calls and mobile data

data.title: UK finds fix for fridge and freezer vulnerability after European hacks
data.description: LONDON, Nov 20 : A British cybersecurity operation has fixed a flaw in the operating systems of commercial fridges and freezers used by supermarkets, warehouses and restaurants, helping protect them from hacks that hit several European countries in recent weeks. A wave of cyberattacks knocked out commercial fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium earlier in November, while a similar hack hit France in October, forcing stores to throw away millions of euros' worth of food. It was thought Britain had largely escaped the hacks because its refrigeration industry relies on different devices, but those working with retailers found a flaw that could have provided an opening for hackers. "We were aware of a small number of UK organisations that may have been affected as a result of vulnerabilities on their systems, and the National Cyber Security Centre immediately took steps to alert and support those that could have been impacted," an NCSC spokesperson said. Following the attacks in Europe, Germany's information security office warned of continuing vulnerabilities in some of Danish firm Danfoss' industrial cooling appliances. French intelligence and cyber agencies accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of carrying out the October hack, which targeted 700 commercial sites and caused 15 fires after hackers raised temperatures in refrigeration systems. The vulnerability affecting British refrigeration systems was identified by consultants at Omega Systems, before ethical hackers from cybersecurity firm Pen Test Partners found a series of additional openings and contacted security services. Pen Test Partners said the operation lasted for about three weeks and was carried out in secret so as not to alert hackers. Before the fix could be made, the affected companies removed fridges from the open internet and prioritised efforts to secure the devices. The NCSC said it shared security advice with food and retail organisations to ensure they took measures to mitigate the risks.

data.title: Honda to recall more than 800,000 US vehicles over Takata air bag rupture risk
data.description: Nov 20 : Honda is recalling 810,592 Acura and Honda vehicles in the US over a risk that Takata air bag inflators could rupture, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Friday.

data.title: Italy gives green light to Tesla self-driving system ahead of EU approval
data.description: ROME, Nov 20 : Italy has given provisional approval to Tesla's Assisted Driving System (TAD), Transport Minister Matteo Salvini said on Friday, making it the first major European Union country to embrace the technology developed by the U.S. electric vehicle maker. In a post on X, Salvini said the decision was "another step forward toward innovation, technology and the mobility of the future". The green light followed "a thorough technical feasibility assessment", the minister said, and came ahead of an ongoing European Union approval process. Tesla's CEO Elon Musk wrote back on X: "Thank you, much appreciated!" TAD, formerly known as Full Self-Driving (FSD), is a so-called 'hands-off, eyes-on' system, that allows a vehicle to drive autonomously while requiring continuous supervision from a behind the steering-wheel. Several smaller EU countries have already taken the same step as Italy. After receiving initial approval in the Netherlands in April, the system was subsequently recognised in countries including Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, and Belgium, allowing Tesla to expand its footprint ahead of a broader EU vote. Tesla also said on X on Friday that TAD had been approved in Italy, posting a video from inside one of its cars navigating the streets of Rome in autonomous mode.

data.title: Waymo recalls self-driving cars over closed freeway lanes, manual traffic control
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 20 : Alphabet's self-driving unit Waymo said on Friday it is issuing two recalls for its robotaxis over incidents involving closed freeway lanes and manual traffic control. Earlier this week, Waymo said it halted operations of its vehicles on US freeways, after a California regulator barred its vehicles from freeways in the state.

data.title: Trump says US to penalize firms building data centers abroad
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 20 : President Donald Trump said on Friday that the US would penalize American companies that build data centers overseas, a move he said is intended to help the US artificial intelligence sector compete with its Chinese counterparts.  "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country," Trump said while discussing AI at a White House news conference following his trip to Asia. He said he would impose a "tremendous tax" on companies that build data centers abroad. Data centers are critical to the AI boom because they provide the computing power needed to train and run increasingly complex AI systems, and a penalty could complicate the global AI buildout. Data center developers often locate facilities close to users to reduce delays for time-sensitive tasks such as payment processing. Transmitting large volumes of data over long distances can also add significant costs. Trump has been a staunch advocate for data center construction in the US, a position that is unpopular with voters. Data centers have drawn opposition in communities nationwide over concerns about electricity demand, utility costs and other local impacts.
